title: Yogi Fills UP Cabinet to the Brim — Mayawati Wants Results
excerpt: CM Adityanath swears in 8 ministers in a caste-calibrated reshuffle, but BSP chief demands proof it helps the poor
body:
Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath swore in eight new ministers on May 10, completing his second cabinet expansion ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections — and drawing an immediate, pointed challenge from BSP supremo Mayawati.

**What happened in Lucknow:**
Governor Anandiben Patel administered the oath at Jan Bhavan, inducting two cabinet ministers and four ministers of state, while elevating two existing ministers to independent charge. The reshuffle brought the UP cabinet to its maximum permitted strength of 60 in the 403-member Assembly. Among the inductees, former BJP state president Bhupendra Singh Chaudhary — a Jat leader seen as crucial for western UP — and SP rebel Manoj Kumar Pandey joined as full cabinet ministers.

**The caste math and Mayawati's challenge:**
The selections were deliberate: three of the new ministers come from OBC communities, two from Scheduled Castes, and one is a Brahmin, signalling the BJP's intent to consolidate a broad social coalition before 2027. Mayawati, choosing not to critique the reshuffle directly as an *internal ruling-party matter*, issued a sharper test — she demanded the expansion deliver tangible improvements for the poor, farmers, youth, and women, and warned it must not become 'mere political manoeuvering.' She also raised alarm over law and order, pointing to a recent deadly attack on a young Brahmin BJP leader in Lucknow as evidence that communities across caste lines feel unsafe under the current government.

**What to watch next:**
With the cabinet now at full strength, all eyes will be on whether the newly inducted ministers can demonstrate governance gains — or whether voters read the reshuffle as election-season optics ahead of the 2027 UP polls.
